qualificationNotes: Expected known answers are copied from independently published sources, not generated by either harness implementation.
RFC 7638 published RSA example qualifies canonical SHA256/base64 bytes only; protocol keys remain P256-only.
P256 author thumbprint DOvxvJiAdIqVWIkFt5hDtCunXLF0BV4-JGv4f-ALSm0 is an independently computed hashlib SHA256 of the literal RFC6979-key JWK, not labeled as an RFC-published answer.
Python native test-only _decrypt_with_aad validates the original sequence-zero CFRG vector, as pyca/cryptography 50.0.2 upstream tests do. Protocol code uses public single-shot APIs and empty AAD.

Java native HPKE validates sequence-zero and sequence-one original ciphertext and plaintext with fixed public test ephemeral material. Random fixture entropy is never substituted in protocol encryption.
Fixed-profile Argon2 wrapper tests compare against a separately instantiated native KDF with explicit 65536/3/4/32 parameters; the RFC9106 primitive KAT alone uses 32-KiB memory, secret and AD.

Public fixtures: author scalar comes only from RFC6979; all other role keys were generated independently using cryptography ec.generate_private_key(SECP256R1). No production key or recovery/password-derived scalar.
